#2060. Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

There remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the new recruits to settle

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It says much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make big improvements, there’s no question about it,’ said the manager.

‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty quickly.’

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several big-hitters to come in without delay in the New Year.

‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

‘Domestic football is really important to the football club, of course,’ he said. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’

The form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’

#2059. Le venete vedono nero: Vicenza e Verona ancora sconfitte. Gallo e Baroni tremano

La settimana intensa iniziata nello scorso weekend per ora non sorride alle squadre venete e ai rispettivi allenatori che non stanno vivendo certamente un semplice viste le voci che circolavano già da qualche settimana e un’altra sconfitta che potrebbe metterli ancora più a rischio.

Da tempo Fabio Gallo non se la passa bene sulla panchina del Vicenza che sta pagando più alto di quanto atteso lo scotto con il salto di categoria. La squadra biancorossa è infatti penultima, reduce da quattro sconfitte in cinque gare (dove è arrivato un solo punto) e con il tecnico che sembrava già sul piede dell’addio a inizio novembre quando si erano fatti i nomi di Sottil, Breda o Castori per la sua sostituzione. L’intervento dei tifosi in sua difesa e il sostegno ricevuto dalla squadra avevano poi portato la società a confermarlo con il ds Giorgio Zamuner che in conferenza stampa aveva parlato di “fiducia non a tempo” per il tecnico e il patron Renzo Rosso che invece si aspettava una svolta pur spiegando di non aver mai pensato alla sostituzione: “Ora abbiamo due partite più semplici e se faremo bene lui sarà sicuramente con noi". Contro un Cesena in salute, attualmente terzo, Gallo dovrà trovare la chiave di volta per svoltare la stagione del Vicenza e anche la sua.

“Se Atene piange, Sparta non ride”. In casa Hellas Verona la situazione è un po' migliore rispetto ai ‘cugini’ biancorossi, ma anche le prospettive iniziali lo erano. La squadra di Marco Baroni infatti era data tra le favorite, visto anche la fresca retrocessione dalla Serie A, per la vittoria del campionato, ma attualmente sarebbe fuori dai play off e lontana ben 14 punti dal primo posto del Palermo e dieci dalla seconda piazza occupata dal Modena (che ha una gara in meno). Numeri che certificano una crisi che ha visto i gialloblù non cogliere vittorie nelle ultime tre gare e venir sconfitto nelle ultime due da Cesena e soprattutto Virtus Entella. I liguri non solo hanno rimontato questa sera i veneti, ma anche conquistato la prima vittoria interna alla settima gara giocata sul campo di Chiavari. Il Verona dunque è riuscito in una ‘piccola impresa’ di cui sicuramente Baroni avrebbe fatto volentieri a meno. Nella piazza cresce dunque la voglia di un cambio con la sfida contro l’Empoli ultimo in classifica che potrebbe essere decisiva per Baroni.

#2058. QPR man will be playing in the Premier League next season, believes EFL expert

QPR swooped to sign the stopper on loan from Manchester City in the summer. He has since become the Hoops’ number one and has made a positive impression with the London outfit in the Championship.

Charles, 21, has made 17 appearances for the Hoops in all competitions to date this season, 16 of which have come in the league, and he has kept four clean sheets. The R’s are currently in the play-offs along with Wolves, Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton and Swansea City, with the likes of West Ham and Sheffield United chasing them down.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on Charles on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “In terms of a goalkeeper’s passing range and ability, I’ve quite simply never seen anything like this with Charles. We’re talking about dropping passes wherever he wants, on a dime, on a sixpence, with both feet, on different trajectories.”

He added: “We really need to enjoy him while we can, I don’t think he’ll be playing in the Championship after this season. Player like this are genuinely the reason why you fall in love with the game.”

QPR’s decision to bring in Charles in the last transfer window has worked out well for them. He has settled into life with the Hoops well and has become their first choice.

The Northern Ireland international, who has 18 caps to his name, was on the books at Sheffield Wednesday from 2021 to 2026. He went on to play 36 matches for the Owls, 21 of which came in the last campaign.

Charles was snapped up by Manchester City on a long-term deal in July. He was then given the green light to head out the exit door on a temporary basis to join the R’s.

City will be pleased with his development under Julien Stephan. He has enjoyed plenty of game time at QPR and is getting plenty of valuable experience under his belt.

Charles’ ability with the ball at his feet makes him the perfect modern day goalkeeper. At the age of just 21 still, he has potential to get even better down the line.

QPR should savour him while they can this term as they eye promotion to the top flight. Manchester City will have a big decision to make on what to do with him when he returns to the Etihad Stadium.

If the Hoops go up, they will fancy their chances of re-signing him again. If they stay in the EFL though, it seems unlikely he would come back for a second spell.

Stephan’s side won 1-0 away at Millwall last time out with Nicolas Madsen getting their winner against the Lions at The Den in the first-half. They are back in action on Tuesday with an away trip to Norwich City.

#2057. Sudtirol, Possanzini: "Iniziare il secondo tempo sul 2-0 sarebbe stato diverso"

Davide Possanzini, tecnico del Sudtirol, ha parlato in conferenza stampa al termine della partita persa per 4-1 al "Barbera" contro il Palermo. Queste le sue parole, riprese da StadioNews.it: "L'inizio del Palermo non mi ha sorpreso perché la squadra veniva da una sconfitta e c'era lo stadio pieno. Dovevamo far passare l'ondata, ma è un peccato perché i miei ragazzi stanno lavorando bene: se vogliamo fare un salto di qualità, dobbiamo mettere più convinzione indipendentemente dal risultato. Se un calciatore è bravo, lo faccio giocare anche se è nato nel 2020. Non è la prestazione in sé che mi farà pensare stasera, ma il fatto di dover essere più convinti. Senza nulla togliere al Palermo che è una squadra fortissima e oggi lo ha dimostrato, non ricordo occasioni oltre ai gol".

"Ci è mancata un po' di convinzione - ha ripetuto Possanzini -. Abbiamo fatto cose discrete, subendo il terzo gol quando non dovevamo: iniziare il secondo tempo sul 2-0 sarebbe stato diverso. Le partite vanno giocate prima di perderle, ma noi abbiamo cominciato a giocare quando ormai non c'era più niente da perdere".

#2056. Fin dove può arrivare questa Lazio? L'analisi di Trevisani e Pastore

Il momento florido che sta attraverso la Lazio di Gattuso non è passato inosservato neanche a Cronache di Spogliatoio, che, nel loro consueto appuntamento del lunedì sera, hanno riservato un capitolo anche al percorso in campionato dei biancocelesti primi in classifica. In particolare, Giuseppe Pastore e Riccardo Trevisani hanno esposto le proprie riflessioni. Di seguito il loro intervento.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La Lazio si nutre della diffidenza e del disinteresse dei media. Io rilancio e penso che la Lazio non vinca a Torino sabato. Ma la Lazio deve temere il contrario: noi che diamo per scontato che vinca, non che pensiamo che si fermi. Con questo profilo bassissimo, che Gattuso è bravissimo a mantenere, la Lazio è sulla buona strada. Aggiungo che per la Lazio è un'ottima cosa avere una Roma così forte. Spingono la pressione verso di loro. “Siete voi quelli forti quelli che fanno 3 goal a partita”. È è il mindset perfetto per la Lazio.

Io è da Lazio-Parma che penso: “Forse questa si ferma” e invece non si ferma mai e gioca sempre meglio.

#2055. Onorato dallo stadio Flaminio alla contestazione: "Lotito ha commesso dei gravi errori di comunicazione. Sulla protesta..."

L'Assessore ai Grandi Eventi, Sport, Turismo e Moda, Alessandro Onorato, è intervenuto ai microfoni di Radio Laziale, in cui ha parlato degli ultimi aggiornamenti sullo stadio Flaminio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Stadio Flaminio? In molti pensavano che la proposta della Lazio non fosse reale, invece il progetto esiste. Si è conclusa la Conferenza dei Servizi, che ha espresso parere favorevole, pur prevedendo una serie di prescrizioni e osservazioni. Tra agosto e settembre la Lazio ha presentato alcune proposte di modifica alla Soprintendenza statale, della quale attendiamo le risposte. Qualora venisse confermata l’accettazione delle modifiche, che prevedono una riduzione di pochi metri dell’altezza, il club dovrà rielaborare il piano economico-finanziario. A quel punto il Comune potrà esprimersi sul riconoscimento o meno dell’interesse pubblico. Si ipotizza una riduzione della capienza di 4-5mila posti, arrivando a un totale di circa 45mila spettatori. Sulla sostenibilità economica potremo esprimere un giudizio definitivo soltanto quando riceveremo il piano aggiornato sulla base delle varianti. Un progetto approvato dal Comune deve necessariamente garantire un equilibrio finanziario, mentre l’individuazione di chi finanzierà l’opera rappresenta un passaggio successivo. Attualmente è la Lazio ad attendere la risposta della Soprintendenza statale. Una volta ricevuta, sarà il Comune ad aspettare che la società aggiorni il piano economico-finanziario. Con il sindaco Gualtieri ci auguriamo di concludere questo percorso quanto prima, perché, al di là di Lotito e delle simpatie personali, l’obiettivo è evitare che il Flaminio rimanga in queste imbarazzanti condizioni di degrado. Abbiamo lavorato a lungo su questo impianto, anche perché in passato erano stati presentati altri progetti. In questo caso si tratterebbe di un investimento interamente a carico della Lazio.

Il rapporto con Lotito? Riesco a distinguere il mio ruolo di assessore da quello di tifoso. Come assessore mantengo un atteggiamento imparziale: non contano le simpatie personali, ma i fatti. Il progetto del Flaminio è estremamente complesso, in tanti ci hanno provato senza mai riuscirci. Comprendo anche le preoccupazioni dei residenti, ma già oggi quella zona è difficilmente vivibile. Le normative attuali per autorizzare la riqualificazione del Flaminio sono profondamente diverse rispetto al passato: bisogna dimostrare scientificamente la gestione dei flussi di ingresso e uscita degli spettatori, la sicurezza dell’intera area e molto altro. Per questo sono convinto che, qualora si arrivasse alla conclusione del percorso, ci sarebbe un miglioramento oggettivo per il quartiere rispetto alla situazione attuale durante le partite all’Olimpico.

L’intervista al Foglio su Lotito? Tutto nasce dalla richiesta di un giornalista di commentare le minacce di morte rivolte a Lotito, alle quali ho risposto sottolineando la gravità della vicenda. Il giorno successivo è uscito il titolo “Onorato difende Lotito”, quando nel resto dell’intervista avevo affrontato molte altre questioni. Da tifoso ritengo evidente che Lotito abbia commesso gravi errori nella comunicazione e nel coinvolgimento della tifoseria, e l’ho ribadito più volte. Se poi si vuole far passare il messaggio che io sia contrario alla protesta soltanto perché sono andato una volta allo stadio per evitare che i miei figli di 6 e 10 anni perdessero l’amore per i colori biancazzurri, credo sia un tentativo becero di alimentare ulteriormente le divisioni. Un’altra cosa che mi infastidisce molto è la volontà di distinguere i tifosi della Lazio in categorie di Serie A, B e C. È assurdo: la tifoseria è una sola, non esistono tifosi più puri di altri.

Posso garantire che ogni volta che incontro Lotito gli ribadisco la necessità di assumere atteggiamenti di maggiore distensione e apertura nei confronti della tifoseria. Diffidate dei politici che sfruttano le proteste per ottenere qualche voto in più, perché trovo molto strano questo comportamento. Per me l’amore verso una squadra è qualcosa di sacro, perché senza tifosi il calcio non esiste. Allo stesso tempo, considero surreale che qualcuno possa decidere per gli altri quali comportamenti adottare. Ho visto circolare alcuni video nei quali sembrerebbe che io abbia sostenuto la scelta di Lotito di togliere il merchandising agli Irriducibili. In realtà il mio ragionamento era diverso: vogliamo che le società italiane raggiungano il livello di quelle inglesi, spagnole, tedesche e francesi? Allora servono stadi di proprietà e il merchandising rappresenta una delle principali fonti di ricavo. Riuscite a immaginare un emiro che acquista la Lazio e al quale viene detto che il merchandising è gestito dai tifosi? È un ragionamento poco realistico. Lo dice una persona che da ragazzo frequentava la curva e che ha acquistato liberamente le sciarpe degli Irriducibili e degli altri gruppi organizzati. Ma quello è un altro discorso. Dobbiamo alzare il livello del confronto.

L’altro ieri abbiamo assistito ancora una volta a scontri tra i tifosi del Torino e della Roma. Per quanto tempo dovremo continuare a vedere episodi di violenza legati al calcio? Chi può essere interessato a investire in questo settore se non riusciamo a renderlo sicuro, permettendo ai tifosi di vivere naturalmente la propria passione? Io andavo allo stadio con il club Re Cecconi di Ostia, partendo da piazza Quarto dei Mille con il pullman organizzato e il panino con la frittata. Sono profondamente legato al calcio romantico, ma se in una piazza come Roma vogliamo tornare a sognare, anche noi tifosi dobbiamo avere un approccio diverso. Perché tanti attori e cantanti laziali non dichiarano apertamente la propria fede calcistica? Quanti politici romani lo fanno? Io, Alessandro Cochi e pochi altri. Perché accade questo? Perché tutto diventa complicato, tutto si trasforma in polemica. Dobbiamo superare queste divisioni: siamo un’unica tifoseria, un unico popolo. Nutro il massimo rispetto per chi oggi protesta, perché rappresenta un grande sacrificio e lo comprendo.

Una data per il Flaminio? Se fossi un radioascoltatore e sentissi un assessore indicare una data, impazzirei. Quello che posso garantire, assumendomi la responsabilità del mio ruolo, è che il progetto è concreto e che siamo agli ultimi passaggi prima dell’eventuale approvazione da parte del Comune. Successivamente l’iter prevede un avviso pubblico, con un ulteriore anno di procedure. Se poi Lotito deciderà effettivamente di realizzarlo oppure no, non posso saperlo: bisogna prima arrivare a quel momento. Ma, una volta ottenute tutte le autorizzazioni, possiamo riconoscere che avere lo stadio Flaminio nel cuore della città rappresenterebbe una grande opportunità di crescita per la Lazio? Credo proprio di sì. Oggi incontro tifosi che mi abbracciano e mi chiedono di non far realizzare lo stadio, mentre fino a due anni fa mi chiedevano esattamente il contrario. Il mio invito è semplicemente quello di mantenere la calma.

Comprendo la rabbia, ma ricoprendo il ruolo di assessore del Comune di Roma non ho la libertà di esprimermi come un semplice tifoso. Quando si rappresenta un’istituzione bisogna rispettare i propri doveri istituzionali. Lo stadio della Roma rappresenta una grande opportunità per la città, e lo affermo nonostante sia facilmente immaginabile quale sarà il mio stato d’animo quando andrò al derby. È un progetto importante perché consentirà di riqualificare un’area, porterà un investimento significativo e creerà numerosi posti di lavoro. Quando alcuni tifosi della Lazio mi criticano per le vicende legate a Lotito, ne soffro. Non certamente per una questione elettorale: se avessi voluto ottenere consensi in maniera opportunistica, non avrei mai dichiarato nulla, considerando che a Roma ci sono più romanisti. Ma non è questo che mi interessa. Sono diventato laziale in prima elementare proprio perché nessuno tifava Lazio e sono abituato alle critiche. Essere laziali significa anche saper essere soli, è uno stile di vita. Ciò che mi dispiace maggiormente è vedere un laziale attaccare un altro laziale. È qualcosa che mi fa soffrire. Non riscontro lo stesso atteggiamento nella tifoseria romanista, che a volte arriva persino a negare l’evidenza pur di mantenere il senso di comunità. Stiamo attraversando un momento drammatico nei rapporti tra tifoseria e presidenza, ne sono consapevole. Ma cerchiamo di mantenere la calma.

#2054. Napoli Primavera, Nocerino: “Mi porto a casa la reazione. Dobbiamo avere una mentalità diversa”

Antonio Nocerino, allenatore del Napoli Primavera, ha parlato dopo la sconfitta contro il Manchester City per 4-1 in Youth League:

“Siamo partiti male. Sembra che quando giochiamo queste partite si pensi di più a quello che c’è intorno, al rispetto per l’altra squadra, e non si pensi più a ciò che si deve fare in campo. Ai ragazzi per il secondo tempo ho detto di mettere ciò che avevano, di giocare, perché non avevano nulla da perdere, con coraggio e intensità. Abbiamo avuto delle opportunità, abbiamo preso una traversa, poi ci sono state delle situazioni a nostro favore che potevano essere finalizzate in maniera diversa. Mi porto a casa la reazione, l’approccio della ripresa, ovviamente sapendo anche contro chi abbiamo giocato. Va dato anche merito all’avversario, sono forti.

Club Brugge? Noi in tutte le partite vogliamo provare a fare risultato, anche lì, se dobbiamo chiudere, dobbiamo farlo nel migliore dei modi. Dev’esserci sempre quella speranza che non deve mai mancare. Dobbiamo giocarcela come sempre, l’obiettivo è fare bene e portare soprattutto in casa a vincere. È un sogno però ci vogliamo provare fino alla fine.

Campionato e Coppa Italia? Dobbiamo lavorare bene e recuperare le forze, oltre a mettere una mentalità un po’ diversa. Dobbiamo cercare di essere più aggressivi, vogliosi, più forti nell’uno contro uno e finalizzare un po’ di più quello che creiamo. Costruiamo tanto, arriviamo negli ultimi metri, ma abbiamo poca cattiveria nel chiudere l’azione. È una situazione secondo me individuale e mentale di ogni singolo giocatore. Noi alleniamo tanto i tiri e le situazioni di gioco, però poi c’è anche l’individualità del giocatore. Quando noi ti mettiamo in una condizione di tirare o di fare l’azione da gol, bisogna avere la cattiveria, la fame di fare gol. A noi manca un po’ questo. Finora siamo stati un po’ troppo ‘belli’, e in alcune situazioni dobbiamo essere un po’ più sporchi”.

#2053. Swansea City identify manager with 2.32 points per game as leading contender to replace Vitor Matos

Swansea City are pursuing a new head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg. Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O’Leary are leading the Swans on an interim basis, but ground is quickly being made in the search for a new boss.

According to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position. Talks have been held between the 44-year-old and the Championship club, and he appears to be their prime target at present.

Alexandersson is currently the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June. He has overseen 14 wins in his 19 games in charge of the club, recording a points-per-game rate of 2.32.

Alexandersson is a 44-year-old coach who has held a variety of roles in the dugout since beginning his coaching career back in 2008. He spent seven years at Leiknir Reykjavik as a player before moving into management.

The Swansea City target started out in women’s football, managing club team Valur before a short spell in charge of former club Leiknir Reykjavik. Alongside this role, Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the Iceland women’s national side.

He then stepped into the men’s setup as an assistant to Erik Hamren and Arnar Vidarsson before a short spell as a No. 2 at Al-Arabi. From 2021 though, Alexandersson has worked strictly as a first-team boss in men’s football.

He spent nearly three years in charge of Danish side Lyngby BK and 11 months at KV Kortrijk in Belgium before moving to SK Brann in Norway. Impressive work there saw him poached for the Rosenborg BK job, where he has continued to impress.

Swansea City head coach contender Alexandersson prioritises man management, working closely with his players to build strong relationships and placing importance on leadership. He has a strong reputation for developing players, which will appeal to the Swans too.

Tactically, his Rosenborg side set up in a 4-3-3 primarily, but he has used 5-3-2 or 3-5-2 formations in the past. Much like Matos, his teams press aggressively in the final third, and he demands frequent chance creation with players directed to suffocate opponents on and off the ball.

In terms of tactical similarities, Alexandersson feels like a great fit for Swansea City. The fact he wants his players to press high and play forwards much like Matos means that there can be a smooth transition into the new management.

Bringing in a boss with completely different ideas could bring teething problems. This squad has been built to play on the front foot with and without the ball, and Alexandersson will ensure they do so.

The Jamestown Analytics influence feels clear with this pursuit. They pride themselves on finding gems in lesser-used markets, and Alexandersson could be the latest top boss uncovered.

After initial talks, time will tell whether the Swans can strike a deal to bring Alexandersson to Wales.

#2052. Lazio, Gregucci: "Gattuso? Ha migliorato qualsiasi comparto: comunicazione, campo..."

L'ex centrale biancoceleste promuove il percorso della squadra: idee sul campo, muro arretrato, maturazione di Rino e orizzonti più ampi.

Angelo Gregucci, ex difensore biancoceleste e storico collaboratore di Roberto Mancini, è stato intervistato dal Corriere della Sera (edizione Roma). Ha analizzato il percorso della Lazio toccando piano partita, difesa, crescita di Gattuso e ambizioni.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Con il Milan, una delle due partite che non ha vinto, il piano partita era perfetto. Mi sembra innovativo, tanti con lui sono migliorati. È un tecnico esigente. So che chiede molto pure a massaggiatori, fisioterapisti e altri. Il merito è suo? Mi sembra evidente. Ha migliorato qualsiasi comparto: comunicazione, campo... Ha cambiato lo status delle cose. Rino non è più solo l'uomo grintoso che investe tutte le energie in ogni allenamento, arrivando a giocare con calciatori tecnicamente più forti di lui. Oggi, attraverso esperienze anche in campionati e piazze che molti avrebbero snobbato, è diventato una guida.

Partiti Gila e Romagnoli, sembrava non si potesse più giocare. Al loro posto non è arrivato Paolo Maldini. Eppure la Lazio ha la miglior difesa del torneo.

Quel giorno in molti temevano la retrocessione. Personalmente a inizio campionato pensavo che la Lazio sarebbe potuta arrivare fra il sesto e l'ottavo posto. Oggi però mi sembra competitiva per qualsiasi traguardo.

#2051. Un grande Napoli sfiora l'impresa all'Etihad: il Man City lo riprende all'86', finisce 2-2

Il Napoli esce a testa alta dall'Etihad Stadium, sfiorando un'impresa che alla vigilia sembrava quasi impossibile. Finisce 2-2 contro il Manchester City, al termine di una splendida prova collettiva della formazione di Massimiliano Allegri, capace di portarsi in vantaggio per ben due volte e di mettere in seria difficoltà gli uomini di Enzo Maresca. Gli azzurri salgono così a quattro punti dopo cinque giornate di Champions League, mentre gli inglesi raggiungono quota dieci. Un pareggio che muove la classifica, ma al di là del peso specifico del punto conquistato è soprattutto la prestazione a rappresentare un'iniezione di fiducia per il Napoli, protagonista di una delle sue migliori serate stagionali.

Il Manchester City prende subito in mano il pallino del gioco e dopo appena due minuti impegna Milinkovic-Savic con una conclusione dalla distanza di Anderson. Il Napoli risponde con due occasioni ravvicinate per McTominay, mentre al 10' O'Reilly non inquadra lo specchio della porta di testa. Gli inglesi fanno possesso, ma sbattono contro una retroguardia azzurra particolarmente attenta, con Olivera e Beukema protagonisti di diverse chiusure provvidenziali. La squadra di Allegri non rinuncia ad attaccare e cresce nel finale di frazione: al 44' proprio Beukema sfiora il vantaggio con un'incornata sugli sviluppi di un calcio d'angolo, trovando la grande risposta di Donnarumma. Si va così all'intervallo sullo 0-0.

La partita si accende nella ripresa. Al 56' Hojlund raccoglie un'imbucata di Gilmour, elude l'intervento di Guehi e trafigge Donnarumma con un diagonale chirurgico. Maresca trova in Doku l'uomo capace di cambiare il volto della sua squadra: il belga semina il panico sulla sinistra e al 67' serve a Bouaddi il pallone dell'1-1. Il City intensifica la pressione, ma proprio nel momento più complicato il Napoli torna avanti: Politano innesca Spinazzola sulla destra, cross dal fondo e splendido destro al volo di Noa Lang al 77'. Gli inglesi si riversano nuovamente in avanti, Gvardiol colpisce un legno e Milinkovic-Savic si oppone ad Anderson. All'86', però, arriva la prodezza di Cherki, che si destreggia tra gli avversari e sorprende il portiere serbo da posizione defilatissima. È il gol del definitivo 2-2, che non cancella la grande prestazione degli azzurri.

#2050. A footballer who loves getting cards! Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo opens up on his passion for collecting as he launches trading card shop in London with Chelsea's Reece James and Levi Colwill

Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

Adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards

The new shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil

'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and said: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'

#2049. Supercoppa Italiana, bando TV 2027 2030: torna la gara secca ma resta la Final Four

Tutte le novità per la Supercoppa Italiana dal 2027 al 2030: si riparte dalla gara secca, ma resta l'opzione estero.

La Lega Calcio Serie A ha ufficialmente approvato e reso pubblico il bando per i diritti audiovisivi della Supercoppa Italiana sul territorio italiano per il triennio 2027/28, 2028/29 e 2029/30, disegnando un quadro che lega strettamente aspetti sportivi e ritorni economici. Il primo cambiamento strutturale è la separazione della Supercoppa dalla Coppa Italia nella vendita dei diritti, una scelta che dà alla competizione un percorso commerciale autonomo per i prossimi tre anni.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Per chi si aggiudicherà i diritti televisivi, la novità principale è la possibilità esclusiva di acquistare anche il pacchetto di title sponsorship legato al torneo. Non è fissato un prezzo minimo di partenza: le emittenti dovranno formulare una propria offerta economica, indicando anche un corrispettivo aggiuntivo in caso di formula a quattro squadre. Chi otterrà questo abbinamento potrà legare il proprio nome alla competizione e al premio per il migliore in campo, oltre a ottenere visibilità a bordocampo, sul trofeo e sulla patch applicata alla manica destra delle maglie delle squadre partecipanti. Sul fronte della trasmissione, le eventuali semifinali potranno andare in onda anche a pagamento, mentre per la finale restano fermi gli obblighi di diffusione in chiaro previsti dalla normativa sugli eventi di particolare rilevanza sociale.

Sul piano del calendario, la Lega cercherà un'intesa con il licenziatario per stabilire il periodo di svolgimento del torneo, ma si riserva comunque l'ultima parola se non si dovesse raggiungere un accordo. Come criterio base il bando riporta la Supercoppa alla formula tradizionale della gara secca tra la vincitrice del campionato e quella della Coppa Italia, fissando un prezzo minimo di 8 milioni di euro a stagione (24 milioni complessivi nel triennio). Resta però aperta la strada della Final Four: la Lega può scegliere a propria discrezione di attivarla in una o più stagioni del bando, con le prime due classificate in campionato e le due finaliste di Coppa Italia (e l'eventuale ripescaggio di terza e quarta in Serie A), incassando in quel caso 7 milioni di euro in più per ciascuna edizione. A pesare sulla decisione tra finale a due o a quattro sarà soprattutto la sede, dato che resta la possibilità di giocare sia in Italia sia all'estero.

#2048. Coppa Italia, la Lega Serie A valuta due nuovi format per i diritti TV

Più squadre di Serie C, sfide secche e diritti TV: ecco le due ipotesi allo studio per il futuro della Coppa Italia.

La Coppa Italia potrebbe cambiare volto nelle prossime tre stagioni. Nel nuovo bando per i diritti audiovisivi pubblicato dalla Lega Serie A, con scadenza al 14 dicembre, compaiono infatti due diverse formule pensate per rilanciare un torneo spesso snobbato fino alle fasi finali. A scegliere quale adottare sarà il mercato televisivo: prevarrà il format legato all'offerta economica più alta ricevuta dai broadcaster, con il via libera dell'Assemblea.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La prima opzione, il Format "A", conferma l'impianto attuale della competizione con 44 squadre al via. Prevede solo 4 club di Serie C nel turno preliminare e l'ingresso delle prime otto classificate della passata Serie A direttamente dagli ottavi di finale con il vantaggio di giocare in casa. Sul piano economico, la Lega ha fissato una richiesta minima di 54 milioni di euro a stagione, pari a 162 milioni complessivi nel triennio. Una soluzione già collaudata che mantiene stabile la struttura del torneo e il relativo valore d'asta per le emittenti interessate.

Il Format "B" allargherebbe il torneo a 56 squadre, portando a 16 i club di Serie C con priorità alle Seconde Squadre (Under 23) di Serie A. Tutte partirebbero subito tranne le prime otto di Serie A (dai sedicesimi), con 24 sfide secche al primo turno, possibili incroci immediati tra A e C e l'ipotesi del sorteggio per il fattore campo. Anche le semifinali sarebbero in gara secca, aggiungendo un turno senza aumentare le gare per le finaliste, mentre le Under 23 non potrebbero affrontare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in finale. Qui la base d'asta sale a 61 milioni annui (183 milioni nel triennio), trasformando il format in una leva commerciale per i broadcaster.

#2046. EFL expert singles out ‘very good’ Wolves man for high praise ahead of Derby County clash

Wolves have handed the winger plenty of game time over the past 12 months or so, despite his tender age. He has become a key member of WWFC’s first-team squad over recent times.

Mane, 19, is under contract at Molineux until the summer of 2029. He has made 18 appearances for the Midlands outfit in all competitions this season, 16 of which have come in the Championship, and he has chipped in with three assists.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the youngster on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Mane we hold to very high standards because we think he’s a very, very, very good player. It is always worth remembering he only turned 19 two months ago. He’s such a young player still.

“If you look at Championship minutes this season, he’s the second youngest player behind Ryan Kavuma-McQueen to have played more than 600 minutes. He’s in a little bucket there with Kavuma-McQueen, who’s still 17, then Mane and (Divine) Mukasa, who has just turned 19, and then Romelle Donovan, who is just about to turn 20.”

Wolves will be pleased that they managed to keep hold of Mane over the summer. WWFC were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

Mane, who is an ex-England and Portugal youth international, was linked with an exit in the last transfer window. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the deadline back in early September.

Many expected the teenager to take the second tier by storm but things haven’t exactly panned out like that. He still hasn’t scored and probably hasn’t made the impact in the EFL he would have hoped to before a ball was kicked this term.

Nevertheless, he is starting to find his feet now and is a promising talent. He will get better with experience and his game is still developing.

Mane looked good against Charlton Athletic for Wolves last time out. He caused problems for WWFC’s last opponents and helped them win 2-1 after goals by Adam Armstrong and Rafiki Said.

Cesar Peixoto’s side are back in action on Tuesday night as they aim to keep their momentum going. They face another match on their own patch against Derby County.

The Rams are in poor form and are in the drop zone along with Burnley and Preston North End. They have won only twice in the league and are five points from safety behind both Lincoln City and Watford after their 2-0 loss at Southampton over the weekend.

Wolves will fancy their chances of securing another win to boost their promotion push as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Stoke City. They are currently sat in 3rd place in the table after 16 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City.

#2044. Jack Grealish's Everton olive branch: Star IS available to return to first team after being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline'

Published: 12:32 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 20 November 2026

Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and said the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He has not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a ‘breach of club discipline’ and a lack of fitness thereafter.

But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night.

Moyes said: ‘He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

‘We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.’

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: ‘He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?’

Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness

Everton have won their last three games and go into Monday’s match sixth in the table.

Asked what Grealish can offer, the boss added: ‘Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

‘But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

‘I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.’

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

A presentation from Blues past and present. 🤝Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a new record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). 💙 pic.twitter.com/tzFuGeUhFW

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

At the start of his press conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a new club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

Moyes said: 'It’s something that I’m really thrilled about but, if I’m being honest, it’s not something I really think about. I understand I’ve suddenly become the manager who’s had more games at Everton than anybody before and that’s a real honour and privilege to be put in that position.'

#2043. Millwall team news and predicted XI to face Stoke City with Alex Neil facing striker decision

Millwall have struggled to replicate the form of last term which saw them finish in 3rd place. They currently languish in 16th place following three consecutive Championship defeats.

Injuries have plagued the Lions’ early-season endeavours, and a run of two victories in 10 outings, coming against lowly Preston North End and Derby County, has left supporters debating whether Alex Neil is the right man to take them forward.

There is no shame in falling to Birmingham City and West Brom, despite poor performances against the two promotion contenders. However, the Lions’ loss to QPR escalated the cause for concern when they were played off the park, not helped by Zak Sturge’s early dismissal.

Stoke City meanwhile are 2nd in the table after four consecutive wins. They defeated Birmingham City on Saturday despite playing much of the second half with 10 men after Luca Bombino’s sending off.

Sturge will serve his one-game suspension against Stoke City after denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity by pulling down QPR forward Paul Smyth.

The absences of Millwall duo Ryan Leonard and Tristan Crama have been felt in the backline, with the latter struggling with ongoing ankle problems while Leonard has been sidelined with a knee injury. Both are expected to make a return at the start of December.

A similar return timeframe is in the pipeline for Filip Marschall, who suffered an ankle ligament injury in their draw to Lincoln City in October.

Mathis Servais was among a number of Millwall’s summer arrivals who generated considerable excitement upon arrival, signing from Belgian outfit KV Mechelen. He has played just nine minutes of Championship football due to a hamstring injury and remains out here.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lisbie; Ivanovic

Jensen started his first game in goal for the first time in two months against QPR, and the injury to Marschall means he has hold of the number one shirt ahead of Max Crocombe.

Caleb Taylor and Jake Cooper have been Neil’s go-to centre-back pairing this term, starting in all 16 Championship matches, and will likely continue their partnership with Mark Sykes set to start at right-back. The red card to Sturge means the left-back role is up for grabs, one which Alfie Doughty could fill against his former side with Jordi Osei-Tutu also another option.

Casper de Norre was withdrawn at half-time against QPR but should be fit to start alongside Jenson Metcalfe.

Promising wideman Kyrell Lisbie has been deployed on both flanks of the attack this term and will likely start on the left, with Camiel Neghli occupying the right as he looks to rediscover the form he showed last season.

Yet to score since drawing with Middlesbrough in September, Tairyk Arconte will look to rediscover his finishing touch as the Guadeloupe international looks set to line up in an advanced midfield role.

The responsibility of leading the line has fallen to Lyndon Dykes this term, but he has been part of a misfiring Millwall attack. As such, Serbian striker Mihailo Ivanovic could come in his place for only his second league start of the season.

Stoke City vs Millwall kicks off at 20:00 at the Bet365 Stadium and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football.

#2042. Update on Watford’s pursuit of Edward Iordanescu as new boss talks stall

Watford swiftly turned their attention to Edward Iordanescu after parting ways with Alessio Dionisi on Sunday. The Hornets sacked the Italian following a 4-0 defeat against Sheffield United.

Yesterday, it was reported that Iordanescu had verbally agreed to become the new head coach at Vicarage Road, with the hope that he could take charge of Wednesday’s fixture against Blackburn Rovers. However, a new update from Sky Sports’ Anthony Joseph states that the Romanian is still in talks over his contract length and has not travelled to England yet.

The club remain hopeful of sealing the deal despite the setback. Iordanescu has been out of management since October 2025, when he departed Legia Warsaw.

He has mostly managed in his homeland, alongside spells in Poland and Bulgaria. A move to England would be the first in his career, should it be completed.

Watford have lost three of their last six matches, with their last defeat against Sheffield United. Although their defensive vulnerabilities stood out against the Blades, their attacking weaknesses have been more evident this season.

Clubs including Burnley, Bolton and Cardiff City have conceded more than Watford this season, while 16 teams have conceded less.

The Hornets are currently the lowest scorers in the Championship with 13 goals. Amin Nabizada is the club’s leading scorer with three goals, ahead of Myron Boadu on two. Furthermore, Watford have failed to score in seven matches so far this season. They also rank 19th in shots per match this season, highlighting the lack of creativity in the side.

As a coach, Iordanescu’s philosophies place an emphasis on defensive organisation. This could help Watford, but they need to improve in the attacking department more.

The Romanian manager, should he join Watford, would bring international pedigree and trophies from his homeland.

However, Iordanescu has been at nine clubs in fifteen years, so he isn’t exactly a boss to build a long-term dynasty. He is yet to manage in England as well, which marks a risk in a likely Championship relegation fight.

Burnley opted for Fabio Celestini in their managerial search, another boss without English experience, and he is yet to turn his side’s form around.

Iordanescu would have the January transfer window around the corner to shape the squad to his liking. His impact will need to be immediate, as concerns grow at Vicarage Road.

#2041. Key midfielder set for assessment as latest Blackburn Rovers injury update emerges for Watford test

Blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training. However, he is aiming to return to Championship action on Wednesday night against a managerless Watford.

The experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer. Morsy has featured on 14 occasions in the league, but is facing a race to be fit in time. On his fitness, caretaker boss Damien Johnson told the Lancashire Telegraph: “Sam was touch and go for the weekend and is similar. He is still being assessed this morning. We will have more news on that after training.”

Meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head. The academy graduate has also been a regular feature with his impressive performances at the heart of defence seeing him keep his place in the Northern Ireland national team.

Blackburn Rovers have been spearheaded by the sensational form of Andri Gudjohnsen, who is only behind Will Lankshear in the goalscoring charts with 11 to his name. But, it has been a collective effort to see them sit in 13th place.

Rovers were showing signs of real promise prior to Tony Mowbray stepping away from the dugout, most notably an impressive 2-1 victory over West Ham before the international break, with Morsy and Atcheson firmly part of that.

Morsy has filled the role as the anchor of Rovers’ midfield admirably and has shown his worth as one of the Championship’s finest midfield operators at 35.

Atcheson meanwhile is at the opposite end of his career, but has been just as influential. He usually plays on the right-hand side of the back three and impresses with his desire to orchestrate attacks from deep.

Both Morsy and Atcheson are vital cogs in Blackburn’s machine and they will be desperate to have the pair available for a favourable-looking encounter against a troubled Watford side.

Hoping to close the gap to the play-off places to just two points with a victory, Blackburn will certainly fancy their chances with the opponents registering a solitary victory in their last five outings.

Morsy’s experience has been vital for midfield partner Kristi Montgomery who is enjoying his breakout campaign at Ewood Park, and his quality on the ball is still there for all to see at 36.

Nonetheless, Moussa Baradji stepped up to fill his shoes last time out, while Gady Beyuku also strengthened his case for a starting berth in place of Atcheson so Johnson has a wealth of options should either of his key players be unavailable.

#2040. Chelsea slapped with huge £150,000 fine after 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' fan chants in last season's FA Cup tie at Charlton

Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026

Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action plan to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

Chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

The club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

In a statement, Chelsea said of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January

Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea stars will show they are not 'soft' after Leeds United rubbed in how often they have bullied their opponents in a video uploaded to their social media.

Leeds produced a compilation of clips of their players leaving crunching challenges in on their Chelsea counterparts and capitalising on mistakes made down the years.

Daniel Farke's side have won more duels than any other club in the Premier League this season, and Alonso's team crumbled when visiting Sunderland before the international break. That was a game in which Levi Colwill and Co were bullied by Brian Brobbey. Colwill was hooked at half-time in that 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin may now be relishing testing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but Alonso said when asked about being seen as weak: 'We focus on not being soft and being competitive. That's our goal. We have played once this year (a 6-3 win for Chelsea in the Carabao Cup). We will play twice more (in the league). We are ready for that. I like that. We will show that.'

Calvert-Lewin shares similar attributes to Brobbey in that he is a traditional centre forward who will challenge Chelsea's centre backs.

'It¿s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9,' Alonso said. 'Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready.'

Asked if defenders have forgotten how to face such strikers, Alonso added: 'Forgotten? No, no, no, I don't think forgotten. But it's demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. This is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don't think it's been forgotten. But it's good they are back, these type of players.'

Only Tottenham have made more changes to their line-up than Chelsea this season, adding to the suggestion that Alonso is still searching for his preferred style of play. Some have been forced on the Spaniard because of their habit for picking up injuries despite playing only once a week.

'Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,' Alonso said. 'I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season. I am sure we will get close to that.

'It (the injuries) is a concern. Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.'

‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’

They added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’

On the pitch, Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash against Leeds United without star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training.

Since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring.

Joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador.

‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’

Chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Alonso confirmed he no longer needs to wear a mask, having been training without it, and the 34-year-old Argentinian could be in line for his first club appearance since his injury.

#2039. GdS: ‘Ambitious, surprising, Italian’ – Milan set guidelines for 2027 transfer business

When building a squad it is important to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

The Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

The difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

It’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the new Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

The idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to plan. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

The former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

Belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

#2038. How can Mauricio Pochettino help Manchester United players to perform again?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to rediscover their winning mentality after agreeing to become the club’s new head coach.

Manchester United announced Pochettino’s appointment just over 24 hours after confirming the departure of Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager is believed to have agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford.

He takes charge of United who sit in an embarrassing 18th place in the Premier League table. They have managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, coming against Ipswich Town.

There is little time for the new head coach to settle in, with a difficult first fixture against fierce rivals, Liverpool already awaiting him.

Speaking to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino made it clear that restoring confidence in the team and improving performances will be his immediate priorities.

“The most important thing for now is to start to work hard to recover that feeling about being a winner – to win games, to perform.”

The Argentine hinted at sticking with the current crop of players to help them rediscover their form.

“We need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for them to perform.”

Pochettino’s first match in charge will be one of the toughest possible introductions to English football’s biggest rivalry. Manchester United travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, giving Pochettino very little time to work with his squad before his first outing.

The new head coach faces a mountain ahead of him. He has walked into one of the most difficult jobs in world football. United have struggled so far into the season and they need results quickly to get them out of the relegation spots.

Pochettino has spoken about bringing back the winning feeling at Old Trafford, but his first challenge will be getting a response from his players who have managed only one league win in 10 games so far. That is far from Manchester United standards and Pochettino will be hoping he can instill some confidence back in the team.

The Liverpool game will offer an early indication of how his players respond to the change at United. A positive result would provide immediate relief for the under pressure United but the longer-term job of rebuilding United will take much more than one match.

#2037. What did the secret drone footage reveal about Manchester United training?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”

The operator apologized directly to the club, its new head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

#2035. I've been to all 92 grounds in the Premier League and Football League and this is my definitive ranking from worst to best - where does YOUR club end up?

Published: 21:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 20 November 2026

Some grounds are beautiful. Some grounds are not so beautiful. Some grounds take you to the heart of the English game. And some leave you feeling like you're on the periphery.

But each of them holds the soul of their community and the hopes and dreams of the thousands of people who make the pilgrimage there every weekend.

On April 1, 2025, I made the trip to Harrogate Town’s Exercise Stadium and first fulfilled the quest of a lifetime by completing the set of all 92 English Football League grounds for Daily Mail Sport. But then Everton moved away from Goodison Park and into a stunning new stadium on the banks of the River Mersey.

I was one short again but on February 23, 2026, I got back up to 92 by going to Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch Everton versus Manchester United. Then, in November, with York City being promoted (alongside Rochdale, whose ground I had ticked off decades ago), I made the trip to the LNER Stadium to make the 92 whole again.

I won’t give too much away just yet, but why are grounds like AFC Wimbledon and Exeter City in my top 20? What about Anfield, Old Trafford and Stamford Bridge? Where does Everton’s dazzling new home rank? Where is the best grub in the Premier League and where did Tyson Fury once threaten to have my jaw broken?

This is my love letter to English football. Read on to find out who comes out on top, where your team ranks and everything else in between – then let me know what you think of my guide to the 92 grounds of England.

Division: Championship Opened: 1993 Capacity: 19,369

Being banned from The Den is the football equivalent of being banned from your local abattoir

I’ve been banned from The Den for the last 20 months, in a professional capacity anyway. I could still go in a personal capacity but, on balance, I think I’d rather not.

The Daily Mail has been told that our reporters are not welcome at the club because we had the temerity to report on the horrendous challenge by Millwall goalkeeper Liam Roberts on Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta during the FA Cup tie at Selhurst Park in March last year, which left the French striker requiring 25 stitches in his left ear.

Let’s be honest about this: there are worse places to be banned from. Being banned from The Den is the football equivalent of being banned from your local abattoir. You don’t have to be a racist, misogynistic, homophobic bloke with anger issues and a penchant for tragedy-chanting to feel at home at The Den. But it helps.

And, yes, I know Millwall are trying to rebrand themselves as a ‘family club’ now and the odd Tarquin and Tabitha stray across the county lines from Blackheath and Clapham to keep it real but that just makes The Den experience even worse.

The last time I went as a supporter was 16 years ago to watch Stockport County play there and the walk from South Bermondsey station to the away turnstiles was an eye-opener.

Not that there were any problems: even at Millwall, football has moved on since the 70s. But this still felt deeply dystopian: for their own safety, away fans walk to the ground through a long wire mesh cage that seems to have no end. It felt like embarking on a tour of Jurassic Park: you know that if the fences fail, the dinosaurs are going to take a run at you.

Inside the ground, which is modern and neat and relatively characterless, the level of hatred for visiting supporters feels unusually visceral. It’s loud. I’ll give it that. It’s primeval. It’s unreconstructed, which can be a good thing, too, and it breeds a sense of togetherness.

If medievalism is your thing, you’re in for a treat. If not, give it a miss.

Division: League One Opened: 2007 Capacity: 30,303

I know it’s a soft target but I really don’t care much for Stadium MK. Or for MK Dons, for that matter

I know it’s a soft target but I really don’t care much for Stadium MK. Or for MK Dons themselves for that matter.

The club was born under a bad sign when it was jemmied out of Wimbledon and moved to Milton Keynes in 2003 and it has never been able to shake the stigma since. The stadium fits the club.

It is a soulless, faceless, gloomy place. More than that, there is something rather forbidding about it. Its 30,000 capacity is too big for the club it hosts and, apart from the joys of the local KFC and McDonald’s, there is little to recommend in its immediate surrounds. Its black seats lend it a sinister air, too.

It’s the kind of stadium only its mother could love. And it doesn’t have a mother. Unless you want to do the 92, give it a miss.

Division: League One Opened: 2001 Capacity: 12,537

The empty end kills a lot of the atmosphere, although the Oxford fans are to be commended for the noise they do generate

I feel ashamed to say it, given that it is my local club, but the best experience I’ve had at the Kassam Stadium was getting my Covid jab there during the pandemic.

When they moved, around the turn of the century, abandoning the chaotic charm of the Manor Ground in Headington and swapping it for an isolated plateau outside the city, they only completed three sides, abandoning the fourth because of rising costs.

A particularly bitter wind blows in off the car park behind one of the goals and, from the main stand – in fact, from every stand – there is a magnificent and uninterrupted view of the Frankie and Benny's in the mini retail park that abuts the ground.

The empty end kills a lot of the atmosphere, too, although the Oxford fans are to be commended for the noise they do generate given they have endured a generation of being stuck here. Firoz Kassam still owns the stadium but not the club. That kind of separation always spells trouble.

Oxford are hoping to move to a new stadium to the north of the city in a couple of years’ time. It can’t come soon enough.

Division: Championship Opened: 2012 Capacity: 62,500

It was a great athletics arena and home to a whole host of golden memories at London 2012 but it’s a dog’s dinner of a football ground

I don’t even like calling it the London Stadium. It’s the Olympic Stadium, but it suited the David Sullivan-Karren Brady rebrand of the club to give it the capital’s name.

It was a great athletics arena and home to a whole host of golden memories at London 2012 but it’s a dog’s dinner of a football ground. It’s also a monument to much that is wrong with the upper reaches of the English game: a surrender of identity and tradition as collateral damage in the owners’ pursuit of profit.

Walking to it, sadly, feels a bit like walking through a wasteland and its odd configuration inside harms the atmosphere even though the fans are right up there with the best in the country. The old stadium at Upton Park was intimate and raucous and intimidating. The London Stadium is nothing like that.

The owners spent a lot of time congratulating themselves on the deal they did to move to the new ground: they’re the archetypes of football owners who know the price of everything and the value of nothing.

Division: League One Opened: 1899 Capacity: 34,835

It is hard to get past Hillsborough's association with so much death and despair and heartbreak and the betrayal of supporters

I used to think of Hillsborough as one of the cathedrals of the English game but since the disaster that claimed the lives of 97 Liverpool fans in 1989, it is hard to get past its association with so much death and despair and heartbreak and betrayal of supporters.

I know, obviously, that this would punish Wednesday fans who do not deserve to be punished for something that had nothing to do with them but Hillsborough, and its Leppings Lane End in particular, has such a cursed legacy that part of me thinks it should have been demolished and that the club should have moved elsewhere.

Even in the last couple of years, fans of Newcastle United and Leeds United have reported serious safety concerns in the Leppings Lane End.

I recognise the flaws in my argument about demolishing the stadium, or part of it, and the emotions it provokes on all sides so perhaps it’s just enough to say I’ll never feel the same about the stadium as I once did.

Division: League Two Opened: 1994 Capacity: 8,203

Sixfields is a soulless ground anyway but its issues have been compounded by redevelopment delays and questions about missing money

It is a soulless ground anyway but its issues have been compounded by redevelopment delays and questions about missing money.

It has the same kind of deracinated feel as so many of the new-build stadia pushed to the peripheries of towns. Its supporters deserve a lot better.

Division: League Two Opened: 1997 Capacity: 5,907

If you visit the Broadfield Stadium, I think you might doubt if Crawley are even in League Two

Not an awful lot to relish about the Broadfield Stadium, to be honest.

Decent fans, of course, just like at every club, but Crawley Town’s home is a bit of a modern monstrosity, next to a roundabout outside town on the A23.

If you visit the Broadfield Stadium, I think you might doubt if Crawley are even in League Two. I had fun when I visited because I was in the away end with Stockport fans but I’m not in any hurry to go back.

85. Coventry Building Society Arena, Coventry City

Division: Premier League Opened: 2005 Capacity: 32,609

Football at the CBS Arena feels like it is in an urban wasteland but it is football, nonetheless

When it was called the Ricoh Arena, I had no interest in visiting what is now the Coventry Building Society Arena because it felt like a symbol of the callous way in which fans of the club were being treated by SISU, the hedge fund that owned it at the time.

But SISU sold up in the end and I went along a few years back to see Coventry dismantle Wayne Rooney’s Birmingham City. Then, in the press room beneath the stadium, I watched as my colleague Neil Moxley got into a decent old-fashioned row with Rooney about his stewardship of the Blues.

The atmosphere inside the ground was lively enough, partly because the game was a derby of sorts, but it is a soulless stadium abutting the M6.

It is football in an urban wasteland but it is football, nonetheless, and Doug King, the new owner, has brought with him much better times.

84. JobServe Community Stadium, Colchester United

Division: League Two Opened: 2008 Capacity: 10,105

This stadium on a roundabout on the A12 in the middle of a retail park is rather a bleak place to watch football

The staff at the club are great, the stewards are friendly, there's plenty of parking, there's a Wendy's next door and the home fans, largely arranged in a stand behind one of the goals, make a superb first of creating an atmosphere.

But this stadium on a roundabout on the A12 in the middle of a retail park is still rather a bleak place to watch football.

It probably didn’t help that I went on a dank March night when a wispy fog lingered in the dim floodlight glare but there was something ethereally gloomy about the JobServe Community Stadium.
