#1941. Arsenal transfer news: Why Kevin Schade could be a smart January signing

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1940. Stupidity or loyalty? Pat Nevin poses key Newcastle United question

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

This follows Saturday’s game against Arsenal.

Plenty of angles to look at and debate from a very eventful 90+ minutes.

Plus of course all of the subplots that swirled around this Newcastle United v Arsenal fixture.

Pat Nevin sees a lot of Newcastle United, the former Chelsea and Everton winger a regular visitor at St James’ Park.

He was on media duties this weekend as well.

Reflecting back on his latest visit, Pat Nevin detailing in the Football Extra newsletter: “I nipped down to a freezing St James’ Park at the weekend, where the reception for their beloved former midfielder Bruno Guimaraes made the weather feel positively balmy. Hell hath no fury like a Geordie scorned, but fortunately the home side played so well in the second half that, at one stage, they forgot to boo him for a good two whole minutes.”

Pat Nevin adding: “I understand why football fans feel this way. Having lost Antony Gordon, Alexander Isak and Sandro Tonali already, it was a heavy blow to lose the one who mirrored their passions the most. Players think differently. The idea of turning down the English champions, who could win the Champions League, and instead stay at a club that is shipping out all of the best talent around you, is demanding an unthinkable level of loyalty. Most would substitute loyalty for stupidity in that sentence.”

I suppose that also sums up my many decades of following Newcastle United, especially when non-football fans ask me why I do it…

Back to Saturday’s match though and Pat Nevin: “Arsenal were fabulous and the gulf between the teams looked enormous in the first half but the comeback after the break could well be my favourite 45 minutes of the season so far. From nowhere, Newcastle bullied, dominated, outran and even outplayed Arsenal. It was glorious stuff. Now comes the tough part as manager Matthias Jaissle has to recreate that feeling every week.”

As Newcastle United fans,, what will our stupidity/loyalty be rewarded with in the weeks and months to come?

At the same time, a gutsy point at Brighton followed by home wins over Man U and the Mackems, then the world will feel a very different place.

#1939. Newcastle vs Arsenal: Team news, predicted line-ups and match preview

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an important role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

Newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

#1937. West Ham striker who is bucking the trend might be on Scott Parker’s radar sooner rather than later

With a trio of front men who are struggling to put the ball into the net, West Ham face an uphill battle to end their five game run without a win with a trip to Fratton Park tomorrow night.

Joel Piroe remains the best of a poor bunch of Hammers front men with four West Ham goals to his name – whilst Taty Castellanos and Pablo have a solitary strike each.

Matt’s article earlier highlighted the woeful statistics of shots per game and goals resulting – the Hammers simply have to do better. Reports suggest Castellanos will be on his way in January to accommodate a replacement.

Closer to home, West Ham already have one youngster who is making waves: Dan Cummings, just loaned out to Aldershot in the fifth tier, has already broken his duck with a strike on debut against Scunthorpe United. Scott Parker has already proven with Finn Herrick’s selection that he’s not afraid to select young talent where appropriate.

20 year-old Cummings had been on the pitch just a few minutes into his debut. According to West Ham’s own web site, he:

“Chased down a long ball on the right edge of the Scunthorpe penalty area before beating his defender, cutting inside and sliding the ball under goalkeeper Maison Campbell with his right foot.

The goal came just six minutes after Cummings had been introduced from the substitutes’ bench“.

If Cummings carries on in that vein he’ll soon be on Scott Parker’s radar: As a third or fourth striker option who is young, fast, enthusiastic, match fit and prepared to chase everything, what is the worst that could happen?

Hitting the target at the moment appears to be a very rare skill at West Ham United: A couple of months’ more with half a dozen goals and Cummings could well have the opportunity of making a name for himself in front of a significantly larger crowd than Aldershot’s 2,252.

#1936. Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund Prediction, Odds, H2H and Betting Tips

Ryan Fletcher is a lifelong GTA fan who runs Read GTA. He's played the series since GTA III came out, followed by Vice City and San Andreas, which he still plays to this day. He's most interested in the technical side of the games and he built the platform Read GTA runs on.

The leaders of the Premier League against the leaders of the Bundesliga, under the lights at the Emirates. That’s the kind of Champions League night we waited years for, and now it’s a regular Tuesday. The champions are six points clear at home, unbeaten in Europe and up against a Dortmund side that hasn’t lost a league game all season.

There’s a twist, though. David Raya is out, so Kepa gets the gloves, and Saturday’s 2-2 at St James’ Park showed that this team can still be got at. This Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund preview covers everything you need before the 8pm kick-off. That means the latest odds, team news for both sides, predicted line-ups, the head-to-head record, the key stats and our prediction and betting tips.

The bookies make Arsenal strong favourites, as you’d expect with this home record in Europe. Dortmund are big outsiders for a side that’s top of the Bundesliga, and that tells you how highly the market rates the Gunners at the Emirates. Prices were checked on matchday and will move once the team sheets are out, so always check before you bet.

Those prices make Arsenal roughly a 67% chance, with the draw around 19% and Dortmund around 14% once the bookmaker margin is stripped out.

Be careful with the scorer lists, because some bookmakers still have Martin Zubimendi priced up and he’s injured.

The big news is in goal. Raya came off with a shoulder problem at Newcastle and Arteta confirmed he won’t be fit for tonight, though he said it “doesn’t look too serious” and surgery isn’t needed. Kepa Arrizabalaga steps in.

Missing Saka is a blow, but Madueke has stepped up brilliantly. He rescued a point at Newcastle and Arteta called him “decisive” in his press conference. Zubimendi’s absence means Myles Lewis-Skelly is the most likely option to partner Declan Rice in midfield.

Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapié; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Ødegaard, Eze; Gyökeres.

Saliba being back is a big boost, and there’s a real chance he comes straight in. Havertz is also pushing for a start up front.

Dortmund had two big worries going into this one, and both look like they’ve cleared. Kovač said Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka trained on Monday and are “ready for tomorrow’s match”. Guirassy missed the weekend win at Gladbach with a hamstring problem, so whether he’s fit enough to start is still a question.

Our very own Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Dortmund and is allowed to play against us. He hasn’t started a game since mid-October, so expect him on the bench. It would be very Arsenal for him to come off it and score, so let’s hope not.

Kobel; Anton, Schlotterbeck, Bensebaini; Ryerson, Nmecha, Bellingham, Svensson; Beier, Karetsas; Silva.

If Guirassy is fit to start, he comes in for Silva. He’s scored four goals in four Champions League games this season, so he’s the man to watch.

Arsenal and Dortmund have met eight times in competitive football, all in the Champions League group stage. Arsenal have won four, Dortmund three, and one has been a draw.

Don’t read too much into the friendly in August. It’s the competitive record that counts, and Dortmund have won just once in their last eight trips to England.

Arsenal have scored eight and conceded only three in Europe this season, with three of their four games away from home. Dortmund have scored seven and conceded five, and they haven’t kept a clean sheet in the Champions League yet.

Arsenal are top of the Premier League on 28 points from 11 games, six clear of Brighton. Saturday’s draw at Newcastle ended a five-match winning run in the league. Eze put us ahead, Newcastle turned it around after the break, and Madueke got us out of jail.

Dortmund are unbeaten in ten Bundesliga games and sit two points clear of Bayern. They’ve conceded only seven league goals, the fewest in Germany, and Felix Nmecha’s goal at Gladbach on Saturday took them back above Bayern. They also showed a bit of fight by drawing late at Bayern in October, although they let a 2-0 lead slip at home to Werder Bremen.

Four straight clean sheets at home in the Champions League is serious form. But Dortmund nearly always score, and with Kepa in goal instead of Raya there’s a bit more risk. The safer way to back an Arsenal win is to pair it with under 3.5 goals rather than paying 4/11 for a straight win. The 2-0 at 11/2 is a decent shout for anyone wanting a bigger price.

He’s the most likely scorer on the night, and Dortmund’s back line hasn’t kept a clean sheet in Europe all season. For those who like the shots markets, Gyökeres to have two or more shots on target at 8/5 is worth a look too.

This is a closer call than it looks. Dortmund score in nearly every game, but Arsenal haven’t conceded in four home games in Europe. If Saliba comes back in, BTTS no at odds-against becomes even more attractive.

Arsenal to win, under 3.5 goals and Gyökeres to score. That fits a 2-0 or 2-1 win, which is exactly the kind of result we’d expect.

Arsenal at 4/11 isn’t much of a price as a single, so plenty of Gooners will be tying the win into a bigger slip. This is a two-night matchday, with more games tomorrow, so there’s plenty to choose from. If you want ideas for the rest of the round, the football accumulators site lists acca picks for both nights of Champions League action, sorted by market and price. You’ll find selections across match result, double chance, both teams to score, goals lines and scorer markets. Prices are checked every two hours, there’s a public results log, and it doesn’t take bets itself, so you still pick your own bookmaker. The picks come from bookmaker prices and not from the team news, so do your own checks, especially on a night when Raya is out.

Our advice is to keep your acca short. Arsenal look a safe enough leg, but adding too many short-priced selections can turn a good bet into a bad one.

Dortmund are a good side and they’ll fancy their chances with Guirassy back. Their press could make life uncomfortable for Kepa early on. But Arsenal are unbeaten in 19 Champions League games and haven’t conceded in four home games in Europe, and Dortmund’s away record in England is poor.

We expect Arsenal to be patient, dominate the ball and grind out a win that puts us right in the mix for a top-two finish in the league phase. Madueke and Gyökeres look the most likely men to make the difference.

Prediction. Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund.

Kick-off is 8pm UK time on Tuesday 24 November 2026 at the Emirates Stadium.

The game is live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK.

Arsenal are around 4/11 to win, the draw is about 4/1 and Dortmund are around 13/2 to 7/1.

No. Raya is out with a shoulder injury, so Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in goal.

Yes. Nwaneri is on loan at Dortmund from Arsenal and is allowed to face his parent club.

‘If it were that easy how were we 9-0-1 coming into this match? What a really odd tactic for Newcastle, get absolutely battered in the first half and then hatch their plan.’

‘That they waited until the second half to man to man press us is just not true. Like not even something that can be argued, just factually wrong. From the kick off they had Steuer and Willock M2M on our pivots, Miley was on Ode, and Thiaw was following Havertz when he dropped into midfield. They absolutely M2M pressed almost identically the whole game. ‘

‘Couldn’t watch the game, but it seems like a decent point in hindsight, especially at a bit of a bogey ground.’

‘Drawing away at a difficult ground is decent enough.’

‘They actually pressed all game. We were just better at creating the situations out of it in the first half. They simply went a bit more aggressive on certain players (man to man) and then the mistakes crept into our game.’

‘Nah they definitely didn’t do high press or pressed with intensity in the first half. It’s more of half press and then fall back to position.

Even in the 2nd half, without Ode’s error I don’t think they can get back in the game. Momentum + crowd backing is a strange thing in football.

Newcastle is a very average team this year, and super young. It’s definitely 2 points drop because of us, not their quality nor Jaissle tactics.’

‘Error from Ødegaard is the clear catalyst for Newcastle to get back into the match. They made triple sub at HT but we conceded barely 3-4 minutes after the restart. Without that error, I don’t think Newcastle score, I think they definitely would have improved though.’

‘Football is a low scoring game. I can excuse one mistake leading to a goal vs an opponent thats 3+ levels below ours. I can excuse a bit of panic as they throw everything at us. I can’t excuse 2 goals in 20 minutes of absolute domination where we’re playing like a league 2 team versus a team that was already playing like a league 2 team. I can’t excuse not putting 2+ versus a team that lies down in front of you the way they did in the first half.’

#1933. Kepa handed Arsenal opportunity to prove he can fill Raya’s boots against Dortmund

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

As previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

As well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the new goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

#1932. A disappointing end to a disappointing match for Newcastle United Women

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.

But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.

Forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier. Both Codie Thomas and the rapid Deanne Rose operated on the flanks to great effect and caused United problems throughout.

They went with a midfield three of Rachel Rowe sitting in front of the impressive and hard working pair Georgia Brougham and Tove Almsqvist. While Norwegian Tuva Espas and the on loan Lois Shooter partnered one another up front and looked lively.

Newcastle United Women made some subtle changes with Kayla Rendell coming back in goal, while Jemma Purfield returned to the back four. Mollie Lambert was given a chance to play in her favoured central midfield berth while Beth Lumsden shifted over to the left wing to accommodate Leanne Kiernan, who was starting against her former side.

Newcastle enjoyed the majority of the possession but clear cut chances were few and far between, with any opportunities that were created seemed to be snatched at or fired over the bar.

The Lady Mags created a couple of opportunities early on, with Beth Lumsden and Lois Joel going close. Before Jordan Nobbs was denied by the impressive Hannah Coan inside the area with a crucial block. Nobbs had another chance soon after, but her effort from a tight angle out wide was claimed by Forest goalie Georgie Ferguson.

Forest were creating chances of their own though. Codie Thomas put the ball into the box from the left, but Tuva Espas was unable to steer her header on target. However, they were soon ahead and with it the game changed over a four minute passage of play.

A speculative cross from Canadian international Deanne Rose out on the left was aimed at picking out Tove Almqvist but it flashed across goal and looked to be ushered out by Kayla Rendell. The goalie, on-loan from Manchester United, let the ball go past her as she assumed it was going wide of her far post, only to look foolish when the ball actually crept in off the woodwork.

Despite that setback Newcastle United Women responded well and from the ensuing kick-off were almost back level. Beth Lumsden playing on her less favoured left flank sent in a deep cross which was headed wide by Lambert.

But moments later Forest doubled their lead, when Tuva Espas forced a turnover in the United half and, spotting Rendell off her line, lobbed a perfect shot over the stranded goalie and into the net from 40 yards out.

Forest could have been three goals to the good before the break as Rachel Rowe worked the ball into the box, but was unable to find the final pass.

Newcastle had a lot of work to do in the second half but it was Forest who were looking the more dangerous side. Tove Almqvist played a ball over the Lasses defence as she tried to pick out Espas in the box, but Rendell was just able to gather it first.

It perhaps should have been 3-0 to the East Midlands side when a brilliant move was started by captain Georgia Brougham. She played the ball into Rowe who in turn found Espas, with the Norwegian international able to advance down the right before sending a great ball in for her strike partner Lois Shooter. However, United captain Rachel McLauchlan got there first and sent her clearance onto the post and very nearly into her own net before it bounced clear to safety.

Forest continued to create chances after that. Rowe curled an effort from the edge of the area and Rose continued to be a nuisance on the wing as she carried the ball with confidence into the final third and won a free-kick. Then did excellently to keep hold of the ball before playing it into the centre circle, to substitute Aimee Claypole, but she sent her effort straight at Rendell.

Claypole, who was on loan at Durham a couple of seasons ago, missed another chance after Freya Thomas played the ball into her feet. Her effort took a deflection before being collected once again by Rendell. Rose had another chance in stoppage time but could only find the side netting.

There were very few clear cut chances in the remainder of the game with Jordan Nobbs perhaps going closest when forcing Ferguson into a low save. Codie Thomas was also strong defensively and prevented another Newcastle shot. While Purfield fired over the bar from close range before sending a corner into Ferguson’s hands.

On what was a frustrating day for Newcastle, one bright spark was the introduction of Jessie Gale who ran her socks off after coming on, putting the Forest backline under rare pressure. The youngster’s cross/shot forced Ferguson into a save to preserve her clean sheet.

With just seconds left of stoppage time frustration began to tell and when Lois Joel shot into the net after the referee blew his whistle she was shown a yellow card, which then turned to red for dissent.

A disappointing end to what was a disappointing day.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Rachel McLauchlan (c), Hanna Németh (Aoife Mannion 88), Jemma Purfield, Kaitlyn Torpey, Lois Joel, Mollie Lambert (Jessie Gale 54), Jordan Nobbs, Beth Lumsden (Emilia Larsson 67), Martha Thomas, Leanne Kiernan (Kathleen McGovern 54).

Subs not used: Anna Tamminen, Hildur Antonsdóttir, Oona Sevenius, Gemma Evans, Abbie Richardson.

Nottingham Forest: Georgie Ferguson, Codie Thomas, Grace McEwen, Hannah Coan, Ebba Hed (Abbie Lafayette 89), Deanne Rose, Georgia Brougham (Freya Thomas 72), Tove Almqvist (Cerys Brown 89), Rachel Rowe, Tuva Espas (Aimee Claypole 62), Lois Shooter (Shania Hayles 61).

Subs not used: Katie Cox, Lucy Carney, Melissa Johnson, Lily Stevenson.

The League Cup has adopted a Swiss League format for fixtures, with only the top eight teams of 23 progressing to the quarter finals. Both Newcastle and Forest were already mathematically eliminated before this game so the result matters very little.

If you ignore the games played against WSL 1 sides Aston Villa and Everton, then Newcastle have conceded five goals in all competitions this season with four of those coming against Forest, who like United are still unbeaten in the league. That suggests the Lace City side should be one to look out for in the second half of the season, as along with Sunderland, they are the best side to face the Lady Mags so far.

A final concern was the standard of officiating for this game. With this being a clash between two second tier sides and a premier competition, surely the standard of the referee and assistants should be better than using ones from the local Non-League circuit. There are plenty of top female officials in the top tiers of the women’s game so surely both Newcastle and Forest deserved better? A referee who needlessly sent off a player in the 94th minute and his flag waving buddies who struggled to keep up with the play throughout the game, simply isn’t good enough.

Newcastle only have one WSL 2 game remaining before the Christmas break, against Watford on Sunday, 20th December.

There is now an international break before an FA Cup Third Round tie away to Manchester Unity on the 13th December with the host team based in Chadderton, Oldham. The Lasses faced the same opponents in the cup back in November 2023, winning 9-2 away from home on that occasion. But following the game both sets of fans developed a great likeness for one another with many Newcastle fans supporting Unity in their games over the past three years.

The following Wednesday sees Newcastle bring their League Cup campaign to a close with current leaders Manchester United set to visit St James’ Park for a rare midweek game under the floodlights.

#1931. Longo: Rabiot renewal, Endrick, Inacio and more – key topics during Friday’s summit

Gerry Cardinale had a meeting with the AC Milan management at Casa Milan yesterday, during which there were four key topics, according to reports.

Cardinale has arrived in the city in good time for Milan’s game against Frosinone tomorrow. Yesterday, there was a summit with the Milan management, including the CEO Massimo Calvelli, Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner, and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão.

This was reported by Sky Italia (via MilanEye) and various outlets, highlighting how Cardinale wants to be ready for the January window and even the summer window. Markus Krösche will be there to help him with that, set to be announced next week, as Gazzetta dello Sport reported.

According to Daniele Longo, there were four key topics during the meeting: the renewal of Adrien Rabiot (which is close), the Endrick pursuit (which is heating up), Goncalo Inacio for the defence, and Krösche’s announcement.

There could be a lot of big movement in the coming months, in other words, as Cardinale is really pushing for these things to materialise. Of course, other matters were also discussed during the meeting but as Longo highlighted, those mentioned above were the main ones.

Cardinale will be at Milanello today and then he will also be in the stands for the game tomorrow, showing his support for the team yet again.

#1929. Former West Ham talisman finally gets his dream trophy after quitting east London

The manner in which some players depart West Ham along with the bad feeling that develops as they press for a departure on their own terms can sometimes be the lasting memory that tarnishes their whole stay in east London.

Such was certainly the case of Marco Arnautovic, for example, a successful forward who demanded a new deal, got everything he wanted, and then quit anyway.

However, with some players, despite the bitterness, the rancorous ending of their career fades in the memory over time, and their stay is regarded more fondly for the highlights rather than the bad blood generated at the close.

Not quite sure yet which category the career and departure of Lucas Paqueta will fit into as his stay at West Ham thankfully fades into the dim and distant past.

Infuriating, gifted, inconsistent, yes, but forever remembered for ‘that’ pass to Jarrod Bowen in June 2023, Paqueta’s ‘yellow cards for bets‘ two year saga became, sadly, the other defining memory of his three years as a Hammer.

Winning the conference League title was his career pinnacle – until last weekend when he finally achieved ‘the ambition of a lifetime‘  (huh) with his boyhood club Flamengo.

Looking on the bright side, West Ham fans don’t have to endure the ‘baggage’ that came with Lucas Paquetá

As reported by sportwitness.co.uk, West Ham’s former number ten referred merely to his time in England as ‘two very difficult years’ en route to winning the Brazilian league title:

““I went through two very difficult years in my life. I decided to come back because I wanted this feeling, I wanted to feel welcomed, to be at the club I love.”

“I have no words to describe what I’m feeling. I arrived at this club when I was eight years old. My biggest dream was always to win trophies wearing this shirt.”

Well done, Lucas. We’re all very happy for you.

It feels a bit like learning an ‘ex’ has got remarried. Good for them. So what? I’m so over them now…

#1926. Stunning from Matthias Jaissle, this is excellent

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Matthias Jaissle didn’t have the smoothest of arrivals at Newcastle United.

Disgruntled at him choosing to move on and United meeting his £9.5m release clause, Al Ahli delaying paperwork so he couldn’t start work with NUFC until only 18 days before the Premier League season kicked off.

A Newcastle United team that had finished 12th last season in the Premier League under an impossible 58 game schedule across all competitions.

Coming in and inheriting a team that lost star players Tonali, Trippier, Gordon and Bruno this summer, then see a Sporting Director in control of a very defined focus on overwhelmingly recruiting younger players from overseas with the hope they will increase in quality and value across the coming years.

Fair to say this was always going to be a season of challenge for Matthias Jaissle.

Returning after the latest international break, the toughest possible matches awaited.

Reigning champions/current leaders Arsenal at St James’ Park, then away at Brighton, the only team to take any points off Arsenal in the opening ten rounds of Premier League matches.

Arsenal turned up on Saturday and did what they have done all season, they suffocated Newcastle United across the entire first half.

The Gunners passed and passed, The Magpies chased and chased.

Arsenal kept the ball, Newcastle couldn’t get it.

Matthias Jaissle’s team couldn’t get out of their own half and once the visitors took the lead, I would be surprised if any Newcastle United fan thought this would be anything other than a defeat.

In 14 Premier League and Champions League matches so far, Arsenal had won 12, lost that game at Brighton, plus drew 2-2 at Bayern Munich.

Apart from those Bayern and Brighton matches, Arsenal had conceded a grand total of three goals across the other 12 matches in the Champions League and Premier League, an average of a goal every 6+ hours in these dozen games.

Ahead of Saturday’s second half, Arsenal had Newcastle United right where they wanted them. Having dominated the opposition and taking the lead, if the home side came out and tried to get back into the game, gaps would open for the visitors to ruthlessly exploit. It is the Arsenal way.

The second half about to start and Matthias Jaissle surprises everybody, three subs at such an early stage. Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Tino Livramento replacing Sean Steur, Jacob Murphy and Amar Dedic.

From the first whistle of that second period it was Newcastle United on the front foot. Going toe to toe with Arsenal, or rather, stamping on their toes.

It was exhilarating, it was what we love to see, what we had seen so many times under Eddie Howe when up against Mikel Arteta. Only Matthias Jaissle having to do it with an admittedly lower quality team, no disrespect and all that.

However, those in black and white elevated themselves as a team, they were greater than the sum of their parts.

Whatever Matthias Jaissle had said to them at the break, when added to the changes made, it was stunning.

Arsenal were clearly not expecting this in any way, United players flooding forward in such a brave high press. Joe Willock forced Martin Odegaard into losing possession, William Osula swept forward with the loose ball and a perfect pass for Harvey Barnes to do what Harvey Barnes does.

An equaliser four minutes into the second half, so sit back and defend a 1-1?

Matthias Jaissle ordering his team to get at Arsenal, drive them back, force errors, potentially more chances…

Just after the hour mark it is Tino Livramento of all people who forces a defender, then David Raya in his six yard box into mistakes that resulted in a corner.

A brilliant corner kick routine sees Arsenal out-Arsenaled, defenders blocked off and Dan Burn totally unmarked, his header parried but Joe Willock doing brilliantly to nudge the ball away from defenders despite pinned by opponents on the ground, on the line, Malick Thiaw smashing the ball home from a few inches out. Wow.

Sit back and try to defend a 2-1 for the next 37 minutes?

Matthias Jaissle insisting that his rejuvenated team keep taking the game to Arsenal.

Those remaining 37 minutes saw Newcastle United created more and better chances.

Arsenal scored a goal on the break which was brilliantly worked but still needed to go through a defender’s legs and a shot that Hornicek should probably have saved. That’s football.

Newcastle United didn’t take any of their chances and so it ended 2-2.

What a match and what an astonishing second half.

This was so so good from Matthias Jaissle.

The coward’s way would have been to approach the second half with a mentality of keeping it tight and running the clock down. Arsenal would have kept the ball for 90% of the time, happy to take a 1-0 or 2-0 win back to London, Newcastle would have been the victims of a predictable loss.

The minority of boo boys were vocal once again at half-time with United trailing to the champions/champions-elect.

By going for it after the break, Matthias Jaissle would have known Arsenal the massive favourites to get a second goal as gaps appeared and it could easily end a very messy three or four goal home defeat.

Yet he didn’t take the coward’s way, Matthias Jaissle went for it and Newcastle United (and their fans) got the reward.

He is for sure still learning the Premier League ropes but I think he has something about him.

Certainly enough to suggest that he deserves a proper fair chance.

The uber Matthias Jaissle critics say Newcastle United desperately need a Premier League proven manager. Rarely, if ever, do they ever name this mythical creature.

What exactly do they mean by Premier League proven? We aren’t getting Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp!

What we would be getting is Premier League proven failures.

Yes, let’s get Sean Dyche in. I can’t wait.

Yes, let’s get Rafa Benitez back and ruin all those great memories we have of how he stood by us at our moment of need. Rafa’s career has fallen off a cliff since NUFC and it would be horrific to see him come back and get abuse when he failed.

All managers have to start somewhere, only a very small handful of individuals who were stellar players then get gifted a top club in their first job as manager.

Matthias Jaissle has done well in Austria and Saudi Arabia.

Now he deserves a fair and proper chance in the Premier League, with Newcastle United.

#1925. Europe's biggest surprise package: Frosinone's remarkable rise as the new Roberto De Zerbi takes Italian minnows owned by Ipswich chiefs to within reach of Europe after eight promotions

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026

Not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone. It is a town of 42,000 best known for many years as the birthplace of 20th-century screen icon Marcello Mastroianni and global hotelier Carmine Forte, but now the talk of Italian football.

Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, currently above Juventus and Napoli in the table.

Armed with the second-lowest budget in the league, they have regularly started with seven Italian players – the most in the league – including Antonio Raimondo, a 22-year-old striker on loan from Bologna, who scored nine goals in 10 appearances before being halted by injury at the start of this month.

The majority owner is New York investment fund Clara Vista, who are part of the consortium behind Ipswich Town, and the head coach is Massimiliano Alvini, who has drawn comparisons to Roberto De Zerbi for both the high-intensity elements of his style and his rise from the humble depths of Italian football.

Only 18 months ago, in May 2025, they looked set to slide into the third tier, bound for a relegation play-off until Brescia were deducted points to hand Frosinone an unlikely stay of execution.

A month later a new sporting director, Renzo Castagnini, arrived and installed Alvini, who kept faith in most of the squad that had survived only by the skin of its teeth. Survival was again the sole aim. Yet from the very first Coppa Italia fixture Frosinone began to turn heads, beating Monza, a team widely tipped for promotion.

By the end of the season, they had finished as runners-up behind Venezia and above Monza who were promoted via the play-offs. It was Frosinone’s fourth promotion to Serie A and by far the most beautiful because nobody saw it coming.

Massimiliano Alvini was recognised as the best coach of Serie B at the 35th edition of the FIGC Panchina D'Oro Awards on Monday

Frosinone Calcio players celebrated their victory against Lecce in October

Much of the credit belongs to Alvini, who was named by his fellow managers on Monday as Serie B’s best coach for 2025-26. The 56-year-old Tuscan played at an amateur level until a serious injury forced him to quit at 30. His coaching career began in the same lowly ranks for Italian football.

He and his brother Walter sold shoe soles for a living. Increasingly, Walter would be asked to cover at work as his brother followed his new passion, travelling to study the training sessions of established coaches, including Luciano Spalletti at Roma and Maurizio Sarri at Empoli.

Alvini remains grounded and stubbornly modest despite eight promotions and the sudden spotlight.

If the season ended today, Frosinone would qualify for Europe but perhaps the most incredible part of the story was improvements made last season by individual players who had barely registered in the previous season.

Notably Fares Ghedjemis, who went from scoring two goals to 15. Also Castagnini signings such as Giacomo Calo and others including Giorgi Kvernadze, Gabriele Bracaglia and goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani.

Frosinone won 3-0 at Fiorentina, beat Cesc Fabregas’s Como 2-0 and Torino by the same score. At Atalanta – the Europa League winners of 2024 now managed by Sarri – they drew 4-4 and came within a whisker of a late winner.

Twenty points from the first ten games recalled the early bursts of Claudio Ranieri’s newly promoted Fiorentina in 1994-95 and Juventus in 2007-08.

Then, in the last fixture before the international break, came a third defeat of the season, at home against Cagliari, despite 29 shots and 13 corners. One of those days when the ball simply refused to go in.

Whether the shareholders of Clara Vista – which bought 80 per cent of Frosinone in the summer – are entirely delighted remains to be seen. There have been suggestions they hoped to see more of the 13 players signed via their data algorithms but only Patrizio Masini and Romano Schmid have been regular starters.

The other nine or 10 names regularly in the starting XI are the same men who drove the climb out of Serie B.

Defensive midfielder Giacomo Calo has scored five goals in 11 games this season

When it comes to the metric of ‘passes per defensive action’, a key indicator of how quickly the ball is won back, Frosinone rank among the top four clubs in Europe. The others are Barcelona, Brighton and De Zerbi’s Tottenham.

Still, Alvini shrugs off the praise. His first seven years as a coach produced two promotions, one sacking and one relegation. Then a group of friends decided to start a club in the seventh tier (the third amateur level) and put him in charge.

In the seven seasons from 2008 to 2015, Tuttocuoio climbed via four promotions into Serie C.

Alvini moved on to fresh challenges. The next four seasons at Pistoiese and AlbinoLeffe brought his first two professional sackings. He lists them openly on LinkedIn, almost as badges of honour, albeit the second was not a conventional dismissal.

Emergency surgery to insert an artery stent early in the season left him psychologically raw when he returned.

Those three years at AlbinoLeffe however proved formative because he was able to watch Gian Piero Gasperini’s Atalanta methods at close quarters. He took that inspiration into the following campaign at Reggiana, taking them back to Serie B after 21 years for his seventh promotion.

Frosinone supplied the eighth and his second taste of Serie A. The first came when he was tempted from Perguia to Cremonese with a team simply not equipped for a relegation scrap. He was sacked by January.

The return is proving sweeter than he could have dared to imagine.

Bad enough that so-called ‘fans’ took to booing Scott Parker’s very first home game at 90 minutes: Now it seems one of the youngest talents from the summer intake is already being labelled as a  ‘flop’.

As they take aim at ..Edwin Austbø who, at just twenty one, has hardly had a chance to get settled in east London before he’s being labelled a’ big money’ (eh?) flop, despite his transfer fee being a modest £11 million. Perspective being everything, that’s about a quarter of a Kilman who cost £40 million and would surely be most people’s choice for the ‘big money flop’ label.

A flop? After three months? With two goals and two assists at just 21 years of age, I’d say Austbo is well on track to grow into the team.

“Expectations were also high that summer signing Austbo could prove to be an exciting addition in the second tier this term….He has two goals and two assists for the Irons so far this term, but you would probably expect his goal contribution numbers to be higher in a team which has scored 38 league goals…..

As things stand, Austbo is quickly becoming a big-money transfer flop, and he needs to improve quickly to start repaying his fee.”

Steady on, guys, This young man has huge talent, was not outrageously expensive and has already produced more goals and assists than players who cost twice his transfer fee. At least wait until the end of the season – his first in the English leagues – before writing him off.

#1922. Portsmouth v West Ham Preview: Predicted XI As Parker Searches For First Win

Portsmouth v West Ham United EFL Championship, Fratton Park, Tuesday 24 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

This is a crucial match for West Ham and Scott Parker, who has probably endured the shortest honeymoon period of any Hammers manager in recent memory. His first three games have produced a rousing comeback against Cardiff City, a forgettable defeat at Blackburn Rovers and Saturday’s frustrating 1-1 draw with Preston North End.

West Ham dominated possession and registered 30 attempts against Preston, yet never really looked clinical enough to score the winner. Indeed, had the referee awarded another 20 minutes of injury time, I’m still not convinced we would have found a second goal.

Parker is still waiting for his first victory as West Ham head coach, and Tuesday’s trip to Fratton Park represents another difficult assignment. Portsmouth have lost just once in eight Championship matches and sit only one point and two places behind the tenth-placed Hammers.

Ordinarily, one might expect Parker to do some tinkering after failing to beat the team at the bottom of the division. However, I suspect he won’t make sweeping changes because he was very pleased with the way his team performed against Preston.

Edson Alvarez – likely to become key in Parker’s plans this season

Parker said he got almost everything he wanted from the performance apart from the result, while describing Finlay Herrick and Edson Álvarez as “brilliant” in his post-match assessment. I’m not quite sure I would agree with that overall verdict, although the return of Álvarez was unquestionably a bonus.

The Mexican looked decent on his return to the team and provided some much-needed protection in front of the back four. Parker has probably made it clear that, for the remainder of this season, West Ham will play with a recognised holding midfielder.

Without wishing to sound like a scratched record, I still believe Jarrod Bowen needs to be used more centrally. Parker appeared to have been given the keys to unlocking West Ham’s attacking potential against Cardiff, but unfortunately he seems to have kept them in his back pocket ever since.

Bowen remains our most dangerous attacking player, yet watching him pinned to the right flank against Preston was depressing. West Ham lacked magic, invention and somebody willing to take responsibility in the areas where matches are won.

Mohamadou Kanté can consider himself unlucky not to have featured at all against Preston because he has been one of West Ham’s better players this season. There is an argument for playing him in the attacking midfield position at Portsmouth, where his pace and direct running could give Parker’s team something different.

However, I don’t think Parker will throw the baby out with the bathwater. He has already spoken about remaining stable and consistent, so I expect Divine Mukasa to retain his place behind Joël Piroe.

Piroe should continue up front, as much because of the lack of convincing alternatives as anything else. Manor Solomon could return on the left, with Parker perhaps deciding that his experience is better suited to a difficult night at Fratton Park.

I suspect there will be a change at left-back, with Ollie Scarles coming into the team. Max Kilman is available again after completing his one-match suspension and should immediately return alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos.

According to the club’s official team news, Alphonse Areola and Kyle Walker-Peters continue to be assessed. Unless Walker-Peters is unexpectedly declared fit, Joël Veltman should remain at right-back.

Portsmouth possess a worse attack than West Ham but a better defence, so this is unlikely to be an open game. They are only two places and one point behind us, while their recent results suggest Parker’s team will have to work extremely hard for anything at Fratton Park.

West Ham’s failure to convert possession into goals remains the obvious concern. However, if Parker can keep things tight defensively and finally find a way to make one of our attacking opportunities count, I believe the Hammers can edge it.

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

Amorim’s plan appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause issues on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a big responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really important because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

“They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I said against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause issues.”

Camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

“Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

“Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini said himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games…

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed…

“That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really important for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

“Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your plan. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

“I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”

#1919. When Football Felt Like Football: A Trip Back to Portsmouth v West Ham, 1992

Tonight’s mid table clash, yep, 10th play 12th, brought back memories of a West Ham United game in Division 1 back in 1992/1993. Without wanting to sound like Paul Whitehouse’s legendary Fast Show character, Ron Manager, and his famous cry of “jumpers for goalposts”, my mind drifted back to the footballing world of the 1990s this morning.

I recall watching the game on ITV, on a programme called the London Match, hosted by Ian St John, and a quick search on YouTube found some footage, with Greavsies side kick being  joined by Glenn Hoddle. Jim Rosenthal was at Fratton Park as part of the commentary team.

Portsmouth featured in the FA Cup semi finals the previous season. West Ham drew 1-1 with Derby County the week before the game, Trevor Morley cancelling out a clearance by Mitchell Thomas which had cannoned off Ludo for an own goal earlier in the game, which kept the Hammers in the top six.

With Billy Bonds at the helm, West Ham were unbeaten in six games, yet faced a Pompey team that had only played twice at home, won both and not conceded. They boasted the prolific striker Guy Whittingham up front, and with Jim Smith in the manager’s seat, were stiff opposition for us. Yet as he said in the warm up the Hammers were one of the favourites to go up.

Pre game the big news was welcoming back Julian Dicks our skipper who came off a three match ban.

The Hammers took the lead just before half time with Clive Allen (main  pic) scoring, yet despite an onslaught of the Pompey goal in the second half they couldn’t add to their tally.

Trevor Morley was denied by the woodwork, while Martin Allen (who was never afraid to shoot from distance) also had a long effort saved.

Happy memories, as it was a time when the club had a greater connection to us, the fans.

I’d settle for a clean sheet and a win tonight, how football has changed or as Ron said “Isn’t it, wasn’t it, marvellous”.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Great days indeed. The London match was the hangover from ITV losing tv rights to Sky. It was pretty good and we seemed to feature quite allot as Itv regionalised live matches. The production was always good as it was made by the same people that had presented the match for first division football for many years. That also turned out in true hammers fashion to be a topsy turned season for us as we got it over the line on the very last match v Cambridge.

That was a season of heartache for Pompey. Missed out to the Hammers on goal difference for promotion and then to Liverpool in the FA Cup semis for a first Cup Final since 1939. That was a great, entertaining team put together by the Bald Eagle.

Pompey fan – I was at that game. Hope you hammers enjoy the old fashioned nature of Fratton Park tonight…but not too much eh?

#1918. Hammers favourite reveals Nuno’s part in his decision to quit West Ham

One of the major disappointments from this summer of change was seeing Hammers’ academy graduate Freddie Potts leave the club where he’d been since he was a seven year old. A ten million transfer fee justified the move in most fans’ minds, but there was still a sense of unfulfilled promise, despite Potts’ finally achieving his dream of a Premier League debut for the team he loved and had supported as a child.

In a candid interview today with BBC.co.uk, Potts reveals why he chose to quit West Ham United.

Without putting too fine a point on it, the whole move to Belgian Champions FC Brugge came about through manager Nuno Espirito Santo’s selection choices and Potts being sidelined, as he explained:

“In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’,” Potts said.

“It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play.”

Nuno’s decision to limit Potts’ game time led to his decision to quit the club

Subsequently the interest from Brugge- now competing in the Champions League against the likes of Liverpool this very week – arose and Potts grabbed at the chance:

“The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

“I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.”

And who can blame him: Freddie lines up against Liverpool this week in the Champions League – the same week in which his old club head for a second division mid table scrap with Portsmouth. Good decision young man. Go and win it.

#1917. Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish star Jesus de Miguel, 30, breaks cover for the first time after tragic accident to pay tribute to Tenerife player

Published: 06:20 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:30 EST, 21 November 2026

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been seen in public for the first time since the tragic accident.

During a match earlier this month, Andorra keeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out Tenerife star de Miguel with a high challenge which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

De Miguel's passing shocked the footballing world and Owono was subsequently given a 12-match ban by authorities.

Both sides have been back in action since the tragedy, but on Friday, Andorra hosted Leganes at their Estadi de la FAF.

That was their first home game since de Miguel's passing, and they made sure to pay a moving tribute to him on the night.

Before the match, the players went onto the pitch wearing shirts with his name and number on them and they carried out a bouquet of white flowers.

Andorra keeper Jesus Owono was seen in public for the first time since Jesus de Miguel's tragic death as he attended a tribute to the former Tenerife star

Before Andorra's game with Legannes, several tributes were paid, including a minute's silence

A minute's silence was also held before the game, while those in attendance applauded during the ninth minute of the match, the shirt number worn by de Miguel at Tenerife.

The most striking part of the evening though was Owono's attendance in the stands.

The goalkeeper has stayed away from the public eye since de Miguel's death, after which he was subjected to chants of 'murderer', but he wanted to attend the tribute at his club's home ground.

Owono was wearing a black coat and hat as he stood next to team-mates who weren't involved in the matchday squad.

Despite receiving the support of the crowd and his team-mates, local reports said Owono cut a downcast figure and that he was seen praying immediately after the minute's silence.

Owono's desire to attend the tribute came after he had also asked to meet de Miguel's family, something he hopes to do one day.

Meanwhile, Tenerife returned to action last week against AD Ceuta CF in a match that was also filled with tributes.

Players provided a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – another nod to de Miguel's shirt number.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars then took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the tragedy.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of de Miguel before the game kicked off.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, de Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place de Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

Owono was watching the game from the stands as he stood next to some of his team-mates

Tenerife returned to action last week and paid several tributes to their former star de Miguel

The tragedy occurred as the game between Tenerife and Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when de Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for his side in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, de Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

Owono's 12-match ban is currently in effect, yet his manager Carles Manso hinted that he may never play again.

He said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'

#1914. West Ham will get back on track if they follow competitor example – report

The difference between success and failure in this division is measured in hundreds of millions of pounds. To the three promoted sides comes the financial mushroom cloud of Premier League cash – a veritable explosion to enable survival in the top tier – but to those who fail to climb out of the Championship – especially those with big budgets – comes financial obscurity and the very real risk of further budget slashing just to stay afloat.

Last season, Championship teams between them lost a worrying £300 million plus: An unsustainable model for football club survival and West Ham, with hugely diminished parachute payments, would face further swinging cuts to stay solvent. So promotion at the first attempt is crucial.

The Hammers would do well to take a leaf out of competitor Wolverhampton Wanderers’ books. Like West Ham, Wolves have stuttered without hitting top form and yet there they sit, third in the Championship. As footballleagueworld.co.uk report, they’ve ground out an impressive sequence of results:

“if Wolves haven’t always impressed with their performances, they have found a way of getting results, and they head into the Derby game unbeaten in seven, picking up 17 points in that period.”

“Wolves are just getting it done. Even when they haven’t been turning up (performances), they’ve been doing enough. So, it worries me that if they turn it on, and click into gear, and reach another level, they could be the ones.”

Winning ugly, they used to call it. And West Ham need to learn the lesson from their Black Country opponents and start grinding out results even if they are not playing fluid, attractive football.

Because it’s all about the points. And what do points make?

#1912. Amorim says Camarda returned ‘in a happier mood’ after Baldini talk and U21 duty

During his press conference earlier today, Ruben Amorim spoke about Francesco Camarda and said that the youngster appeared much happier after returning from international duty.

It hasn’t been an easy season for Camarda so far, getting a mere 119 minutes on the pitch, after initially believing that he would get a lot more. Luckily, he managed to boost his confidence during the international break, scoring for Italy’s U21 side against France.

He could perhaps use that to turn a corner, though everything depends on how much playing time Ruben Amorim is willing to give him. The feeling is that there isn’t loads up for grabs, which is why the loan rumours are heating up too.

During the press conference ahead of Milan-Frosinone earlier this afternoon, Amorim was asked about Camarda and what the next steps are for him. He confirmed that everything is up in the air, but also said that the youngster is now in a much better mood.

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length, and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now,” he stated.

It seems Silvio Baldini really did do wonders with his man-to-man talk with Camarda during the break.

#1911. Report – West Ham prepared to cut their losses on January exit that suits all parties

From the sound of it, West Ham United are going all-in to refresh their options in front of goal in January. The club face a crisis with none of their trio of goal scorers looking fit for purpose: The best of the three, Joel Piroe, has amassed four goals this season whilst the other two have managed just one goal apiece.

Neither Pablo Felipe nor Taty Castellanos have fulfilled the expectations that were present when they were signed in the January window at the start of this year – Taty especially was expected to boss the Championship after the Hammers were relegated but at times he’s appeared no more than a scowling misfit, unable to influence games when he’s been called upon.

‘What a waste of money” as the song goes…

Footballinsider.com – who are usually on the ball with their reporting – have it apparently on good authority that West Ham are prepared to sanction his departure in January even though the club will have to absorb yet another huge financial hit:

“Sources: West Ham to accept Taty Castellanos loss ahead of January”

Runs their article, detailing West Ham’s willingness to sell the forward, despite being fully aware that they’ll not see anything like the £26 million they paid for the Argentine striker just twelve months ago:

“The 28-year-old has scored just one goal from 15 games in the Championship this season, and is performing way below the level West Ham expected from him.

Sources say that the East London outfit are prepared to sell Castellanos at a loss this winter, knowing that it will be “very difficult” to recoup the £26million they paid for him.”

This is the key: Taty had previously been linked with loan moves back to Argentina which were never really feasible. The fact that West Ham are apparently putting it ‘out there’ that they’ll take the hit in order to move the striker on means that bids should be forthcoming in the winter market from a number of clubs; several who’ll no doubt chance their arm hoping to get him for a bit of a steal.

One goal in 15 games in the second division is nothing to write home about though, and so West Ham’s approach is borne largely out of facing the undeniable fact that Castellanos has been a massive disappointment, not to mention a colossal waste of money.

#1909. A very positive record: Luca Pairetto will officiate Milan’s game against Frosinone

Luca Pairetto has been assigned to the game between AC Milan and Frosinone on Sunday evening, which is good news for the Rossoneri.

Ruben Amorim and his men will be looking to make it three consecutive wins against Frosinone, after beating Inter and Genoa before the international break. It might not be such an easy task, though, as admitted by the gaffer himself in his press conference.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Frosinone have indeed started the season well, currently sitting in sixth place, and they don’t really have anything to lose from their trip to San Siro. Only something to gain, which can always make things tricky for the favourite.

Given the above, as always, Milan will be hoping for good officiating to keep the away side from disrupting the play too much. The Italian Referees Association, also known as AIA, announced the referees for this weekend’s game a few days ago and for the Rossoneri, it will be Luca Pairetto.

The 42-year-old is definitely one of the more experienced referees around, even if he has never reached the heights of some of his colleagues. In any case, he has officiated 12 games involving Milan so far and the record is positive: 9 wins, 2 draws and 1 defeat.

It’s been a while since he last officiated a Milan game, though, as we have to go back to the 2024-25 season. The Rossoneri played Empoli and beat them 2-0, courtesy of goals from Rafael Leao and Santiago Gimenez.

Despite the win, the game wasn’t without controversy. A red card was not given to Empoli despite a reckless challenge, and Fikayo Tomori was then given a second yellow when the whole sequence should have been stopped due to offside.

However, most of those errors were made by VAR or the assistant referee and not Pairetto himself.
